notes: PEAK SEASON: Dec-Feb is Siem Reap's dry, cool high season - book accommodation 6-9 months ahead (i.e., by ~Apr-Jun 2026) for the best villa inventory; expect 20-40% above shoulder-season rates (reflected above). ACCESSIBILITY BIG PICTURE: Siem Reap is one of SE Asia's more doable temple towns for a mobility scooter IF you use a private A/C van (not tuk-tuks) - Angkor Wat's ground enclosure is reachable via the causeway ramps, Bayon's lower terraces via the smoother east approach, and Ta Prohm has flat jungle paths with wooden boardwalks; ALL upper temple tiers are steep steps and off-limits to wheels. Cambodia Wheelchair Rental ($60/day incl. assistant) and Roll In Asia are the two established accessible operators. Sofitel, Park Hyatt and Raffles are the most reliably step-free stays (elevators/ground-floor rooms); Phum Baitang's stilted villas are the accessibility trap to avoid. VERIFICATION CAVEATS: All booking URLs returned HTTP 200 with a browser user-agent EXCEPT: Vrbo listing (7895945ha) returned 429 rate-limit to bots but is a live listing surfaced by Vrbo's own search (8BR, sleeps 16, ~$440/night avg); GetYourGuide and hyatt.com return 403 to bots (Cloudflare) but URLs come from their live indexed inventory. Airbnb was skipped per bot-block guidance - the same 8BR/5BR villas appear on Vrbo/Agoda. PRICING KEY: 'listed' = price published on a live page/snippet at research time (Jul 2026); 'estimated' = triangulated from published base rates + typical Dec-Feb peak uplift; re-quote exact dates at booking. BUDGET REALITY CHECK: comfort tier villas ($300-600 total/night) comfortably beat hotels on space for 9; the premium hotels require 3-4 rooms/a villa+rooms combo and land $1,200-2,600/night. Angkor pass math for this family: 7 payers (6 adults + the 15yo; the 7yo and 1yo enter free) - 3-day pass x7 = $434.
